fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses AlCoCrFeNi rather than the target HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy.
It proposes stationary friction processing and grain refinement instead of the target silicide coating used for oxidation resistance.
The proposed Cr2O3/Al-rich oxide mechanism does not reconstruct the target self-healing silicide-scale mechanism involving (Zr,Hf)O2 filling.
The cited evidence directly supports the alternative AlCoCrFeNi hypothesis but provides no evidence for transfer to the target HfNbTaTiZr system.
explanation: This is a scientifically supported alternative oxidation-resistance strategy, with direct evidence that ultrafine grains reduce oxidation kinetics in AlCoCrFeNi under the stated conditions. Its baseline comparison and falsification experiment are reasonable, although the boundary statement is underspecified. It does not reconstruct the hidden target: the alloy, processing route, oxidation treatment, protective-scale chemistry, and magnitude of improvement are all different. Agreement is limited to the broad objective of reducing high-temperature oxidation through formation of a protective oxide barrier.
